classification.difficultyReason: Convert the mixed units, identify the trapezium, rectangle and semicircle, infer the semicircle radius from the board width, then subtract the circular hole and round.

inlines.text: The front of a grandfather clock consists of a timber board with dimensions as shown.
A circle of radius 20 cm is cut from the board to form the clock face.
Find the remaining area of the timber board correct to one decimal place.

spec.description: Upright board with a semicircular top, rectangular middle and shallow trapezium widening towards its bottom. A circular cutout has a centre dot, dashed radius and curved 20 cm leader. The rectangle height dimension is 0.8 m; the rectangle–trapezium boundary is dashed and labelled 60 cm. The lower trapezium has height 5 cm and bottom width 64 cm.
spec.mathematics: The rectangular middle is 60 cm wide and 80 cm high. The top semicircle has diameter 60 cm. The lower trapezium has parallel sides 60 cm and 64 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm. The circular cutout has radius 20 cm. Drawing proportions follow the source illustration rather than a common numerical scale.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and construction cues are visible; no component areas, inferred radius or final answer is printed.

answer.worked:
Convert the rectangle height: $0.8\text{ m}=80\text{ cm}$. The top semicircle has radius $60\div2=30\text{ cm}$.

$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{bottom trapezium}}&=\frac{5(64+60)}{2}\\
A_{\text{bottom trapezium}}&=310\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{middle rectangle}}&=80\times60\\
A_{\text{middle rectangle}}&=4800\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{top semicircle}}&=\frac{\pi(30)^2}{2}\\
A_{\text{top semicircle}}&=450\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{hole}}&=\pi(20)^2\\
A_{\text{hole}}&=400\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{remaining}}&=310+4800+450\pi-400\pi\\
A_{\text{remaining}}&=5110+50\pi\text{ cm}^2\\
A_{\text{remaining}}&\approx5267.1\text{ cm}^2
\end{align*}$$

The remaining area is $5267.1\text{ cm}^2$, correct to one decimal place.
